text:
Avery: Heads up — starter app (python quickstart) returned partial streaming tokens then a 402 mid-stream. First call looked successful, then stream cut and client shows "billing_required".
mika: ugh. which SDK version and sample repo? also paste the exact curl that fails if possible.
onboard-bot: FYI: Your workspace "acme-dev" trial ended 3 days ago. Streaming endpoints now require an active billing method. See https://app.redwood.ai/orgs/acme-dev/billing
Avery: SDK: redwood-python 0.9.2, sample: starter-chat demo. Repro with streaming: `curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/chat/generate?stream=true" -d '{"input":"hello"}'`
mika: try `-i` to see response headers. If server sends 402 mid-stream it's probably a preflight decision for long outputs.
DevOpsGuru: check `x-rw-trial-state` and `x-rw-reason` headers. We recently gated streaming on trial expiry to prevent surprise costs. If you see `x-rw-reason: billing_required` that's the indicator.
Avery: got it — header shows `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` then later a chunk with `HTTP/1.1 402 Payment Required` (weird ordering). Paste of response body chunk: `{"error":{"code":"billing_required","message":"enable billing to continue streaming"}}`
Sam: order matters — some proxies send initial 200 for handshake then a control event inserts billing error. Workaround: use non-streaming generation (`stream=false`) which returns a proper 402 at the start instead of mid-stream.
mika: can also set `max_tokens` low while you sort billing, or call a fallback model on failure. Example fallback header logic in the node SDK:

```js
// pseudo
client.on('chunk', (c) => process.stdout.write(c))
client.on('error', async (err) => {
  if (err.code === 'billing_required') {
    // switch to light fallback
    await client.generate({ model: 'rwd-small-fallback', input: prompt })
  }
})
```

Sam: added a short note to the quickstart README about this gating + precheck to call `GET /v1/orgs/me/billing_status` before streaming to provide a nicer UX.
Avery: thanks — that precheck will save customers. Can we make the SDK bubble this error earlier (before opening SSE) so example apps don't show partial output?
mika: filing a tiny DX ticket to make the Python SDK check billing status before opening a persistent stream. @DevOpsGuru can you review the telemetry/edge-case? :pray:
DevOpsGuru: will take a look, probably a small change in stream manager to query metadata first. For now adding README note + sample fallback is a good mitigation. :+1:
Avery: ok closing for now, leaving the logs and curl in the thread if anyone needs them.
